Timing trend (median, contained showers, 3&9 GeV anchors): σ_t ≈ 323/√E ⊕ 79 ps — the constant term nearly half of LuAG’s 138 ps, references included unsubtracted. The 9 GeV point (133 ± 5 ps) is the best timing of the campaign; its 516 ps mean against the 133 ps median is the strongest daytime-outlier rescue yet. DSB1 delivers ~2.1× the LuAG light (~1,250–1,390 ADC-eq/GeV): the scan histograms extend to 16k and at 11 GeV the summed response approaches the ~13.6k LG headroom ceiling (rails still <0.02%). Containment floors 0/1500/4000/6000/6500 from the measured spectra. High-energy response flattening mirrors LuAG — the cross-run gain ladder and shower-max migration (see the LuAG page’s linearity forensics), plus the LG ceiling at 11 GeV.

Run-specific notes

everything unique to this run

Coincidence 66.6–69.7% = the e+μ+π content of the positive 5 GeV beam (67.5% from the T10 tables) — quantitative proof the 1.5 bar tag radiates on pions. The 508 ps “shower time” of the tagged sample is the hadronic giveaway. As an electron point this run is dead (run 37 at 0.400/0.405 bar replaces it); it survives as a π-enriched control sample and the fastest MIP set of the campaign (20k in 11 minutes).

Run-specific notes

everything unique to this run

This is the run diagnosed live in FINDINGS (“1 GeV rate mystery”): it began in the 11 GeV tight-slit config with ~17% X₀ of XCET gas in the line (33 trig/min, beam wider than the profile monitor) and recovered after the mid-run pressure bleed + collimator opening. The tag is immune to the change (plateau flat to thr 200 at both pressures): 86.6% coincidence = the 1 GeV e⁻ content. Beam width and rate differ across the boundary — miss fraction 66.2% overall, dominated by the pre-fix hours. A stable overnight 1 GeV retake is being taken; treat this run as the backup, sliced at the config boundary if used.
